metadata.note: Modern-day NJ Transit Rail network, as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://www.njtransit.com/rail_data.zip. Route geometry, frequency (headway_min, from real scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday), and avg_speed_kmh (from real scheduled trip duration) are all sourced directly from the agency's own GTFS feed, same methodology as data/amtrak.geojson. Each route is a single-year segment (2026) since GTFS has no historical depth. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added by estimating headway_min at researched ownership/frequency-milestone boundaries (predecessor-railroad origin dates, DL&W/PRR/Erie/CNJ corporate history, 1930-1933 electrification programs, the 1976 Conrail and 1983 NJ Transit takeovers, etc., sourced from Wikipedia and railroad-history sites); unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment, these older headway numbers are not derived from real historical timetables and should be read as illustrative estimates, not precise data. GEOMETRY UPGRADED 2026-08-23: the Port Jervis Line (njt-6) shares the same physical track as the historic Erie Railroad main line (see erie_railroad_mainline.geojson) for the entire stretch from Port Jervis down to around Rutherford, NJ -- confirmed by comparing the two independently-traced geometries, which sat within 10-270m of each other along that whole corridor (i.e. functionally the same track). Since erie_railroad_mainline.geojson's OpenStreetMap-traced geometry (887 points) is far denser/more precise than NJ Transit's own GTFS shape (49 points for the whole line), that Port Jervis-Rutherford stretch was replaced here with the denser real-traced geometry, spliced at the point (near Rutherford) where the two lines' real routing actually diverges -- the Port Jervis Line continues via the Bergen County Line into Hoboken/Secaucus, while the historic Erie main line (as traced in that file) heads to its original Jersey City terminal instead. The unique Hoboken/Secaucus-bound final stretch is unchanged, still from NJ Transit's own GTFS shape.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
